newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cocoa steadies but may be vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cocoa steadies but may be vulnerable.

text.p: World cocoa prices steadied on Wednesday but traders said they may weaken again soon extending a brisk fall of earlier this week.

On the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) cocoa market the September futures contract had dropped by 19 pounds sterling a tonne to 994 on Tuesday in a speculator sell-off and word of beneficial rain in Ivory Coast, the top producer.
Wednesday saw the market steadier, just above 1,000 sterling, helped by a decline in the value of sterling.
But New York futures eased whilst German processors were said by Hamburg traders to have no plans just now to revise buying targets for both cocoa beans and butter which are below current offers.
"Consumers may not come back into the market this month until their price ideas are met," one trader said. "Alternatively, we would need fresh news on Ivorian crops to move the market either way."
A weather pattern generated by the El Nino Pacific Ocean current could bring dry weather to West Africa, crop experts say, but they now add that it might be offset by generally higher output.
Coffee prices were again easier in New York-led technical selling and wheat prices firmed but commodity prices generally were rangebound on Wednesday.

Iraqi Oil Minister Mohammed Rasheed said he expected oil exports to resume by mid-August after final details on an accord to restart U.N.-supervised sales fell into place at the United Nations on Tuesday.

Traders anticipated that oil prices may ease when the new volumes from Iraq reach markets. The short-term key will be Iraqi export capacity. Analysts estimate Iraq is capable of moving some 1.3-1.4 million barrels per day.
